as_told.title: Plutarch names Sonchis, elder priest of the Temple of Sais, as Solon's source for the Atlantis story

plain: The claim is that the Greek writer Plutarch named the Egyptian priest who knew the Atlantis story: an elder priest called Sonchis at the temple of Sais in Egypt. Matt LaCroix, a researcher of ancient history, tells it, pointing to Plutarch's Lives. In Plutarch, he says, "there was a very specific elder priest at the temple" in Egypt with that name. Plato's account says that the Athenian lawmaker Solon heard of Atlantis from priests in Egypt. LaCroix's point is that Plutarch goes further and names "a specific individual in history," the elder priest "who had all the knowledge," with "all the other ones" supporting him. LaCroix is the only teller. He makes the point twice in the same conversation, and the second time says outright that Sonchis was Solon's source. It matters to him because a named priest would make the Atlantis account look less like Plato's invention and more like a chain of real people passing on old knowledge.
